messages:
leah: Quick thread — after onboarding int4 variant (model: rwdx-13b-int4, config rope_scale=1.15) I see reproducible divergence when context > 12k. Float16 stays stable. Repro script: `scripts/repro/longwrap.sh` :eyes:
arjun: Can you paste minimal repro input? Is this on dedicated or local dev?
leah: Dedicated dev cluster (gpu-pool-dev-3), seq length 20k, repeated anchor paragraph + trailing question. Command:
```
./run_eval --model rwdx-13b-int4 --rope-scale 1.15 --input tests/anchors/long_anchor.txt --seed 42 --max-tokens 2048
```
Output diff at token 12345: tokens mismatch and then subsequent softmax probs diverge by >1e-2.
sam: Any cache eviction logs? Maybe KV sliding window rolled at different offset with int4 packer?
leah: Yes, found this in logs: `kvcache: evicted prefix at pos=12288 reason=sliding-window-start`, then a few microseconds later `kvcache: prefill-handshake mismatch fingerprint=0x7a3b`. Appears like handshake (warmstart) sees off-by-one when quantized.
pablo: Did we change the rotary base or scaling code in quant path? Int4 kernel uses scaled-rotary-fastpath (PR #487). @arjun ^
arjun: I suspected that. The int4 path applies per-shard pre-scaling to reduce saturation. There might be a rounding in the fastpath that shifts the effective rotation phase for anchors. Will bisect.
maya: I ran a quick float16 -> int4 token-by-token diff. The first differing token is introduced when KV index wrapped from 12287->12288. Looks like "anchor shelf" (terming it now) where stored key position + aliasing causes interpolation mismatch.
leah: Repro artifacts: small script that resends same anchor but with an extra newline before trailing question - that *fixes* it. So off-by-one behavior sensitive to prompt layout.
sam: That's interesting — suggests indexing vs alignment. Can you dump kv-indexes + rot-angles around the window? Maybe add `KV_INDEX_DUMP=1` env.
leah: Will do and push logs to https://internal.s3/redwood/tests/int4-anchor-drift/1719504321.log
ci-bot: CI run started: long-context-regression/int4-anchor-drift (job 2548). Logs will be available in ~30m.
arjun: I'll start a bisect between PR 482 (int4 packer) and 487 (rotary-fastpath). If someone can run the same repro with `rope_scale=1.0` vs `1.15` that'd be helpful.
pablo: On it. Running both now on dev3. ETA ~10m.
maya: Note for eval team: add a permutation test — shuffle anchor paragraphs to see if it's position dependent.
leah: Thanks. If we can get kv dumps we can see whether prefill handshake fingerprint differs due to quantized rounding of sin/cos tables. Could be LUT quantization.
sam: Good point — also check whether caching handshake uses hash of raw embeddings vs quantized keys; mixing those would cause mismatch.
arjun: Update: bisect points to rotary-fastpath (PR 487). Replacing with fallback to scalar rotation fixes reproduction. We need a precise patch — possibly compute rot angles in float32 before quantization.
leah: Filed issue #INC-934: "int4 rotary-fastpath introduces anchor-shelf drift at high context" with repro + logs.
pablo: After running on rope_scale=1.0 int4 still diverges but later (around 18k), guessing scale amplifies error. We should run with quantized sin/cos tables vs full precision to confirm.
maya: TL;DR: root cause likely accumulation of small phase rounding + an off-by-one alias due to window eviction boundary. Plan: kv dump + numeric compare + temp revert PR 487 on prod-dedicated; schedule patch.
leah: Agreed. tagging follow-ups: @arjun please produce fix PR, @sam add regression test in long-context suite, @maya add permutation tests to eval harness. Will monitor CI.
arjun: ack. I'll post PR link when ready.
sam: adding test now.
ci-bot: CI run complete: job 2548 — failed (check kv-dump artifacts). https://ci.redwood/in/2548
leah: Thanks all. Will watch artifacts and confirm once PR lands. :thumbsup:
